result:
Solution 3 is most likely correct, though I did not fully prove its key step.

Solutions 1 and 2 both assume the incircle is tangent to ω₂ and ω₃. The Sawayama–Thébault theorem says only that the incenter lies on the line O₂O₃, not that the incircle touches those circles. So their equations are unjustified and their answers (495/2 and 13) are unreliable.

The setup shared by all three solutions is sound. Put D at the origin with BC on the x-axis, and let t = tan(∠ADC/2). Then O₂ = (−5t, 5) and O₃ = (7/t, 7). The condition |O₂O₃| = 13 gives 5t + 7/t = √165.

By Thébault, I lies on segment O₂O₃ at height r, which is between 5 and 7. It divides that segment in the ratio (r−5):(7−r). Solution 3 claims this ratio equals 5:7, the ratio of the radii. That would make I the internal center of similitude of ω₂ and ω₃, and it gives r = 35/6.

I checked this in the symmetric case, where D is the midpoint of an isosceles triangle. There the radii are equal and I is the midpoint of O₂O₃, so the claim holds. I did not verify it in general, and Solution 3's derivation of it is only sketched. Still, it is the only candidate consistent with the correct form of the theorem, and its value 35/6 lies in the required range (5, 7).

CHOICE: 3
